title: Your tier 2 costs more up front and less per month, and every owner read it as a typo
body: a month. Tier 2 is $3,500 setup and
a month. Eight of the ten owners stopped on that line, and several said it was the thing they would email to ask about before agreeing to a call.

This is not a prototype bug. It is the real price list, and the page is showing it faithfully. But a buyer scanning a table reads the cheaper monthly on the more expensive tier as a mistake, and doubting the price is a bad place to spend the attention you just earned. Either explain it in the row, or reprice.

title: The prose went, the lists did not. They came back as chips, flags and table rows
body: The instruction was fewer bullets and more visual explanation. What largely happened is that bullet lists were
as tick flags, status chips, spec rows and table cells. One page has seven status chips in a row; another was called out for a proof section that is six sentences wearing a table.
Worth deciding what visual explanation actually means to you, because right now a lot of the ten deleted words without reducing the number of things the eye has to read.

title: They want to know who pulls the patient list
body: Three owners asked, without being asked, who runs the export each month and what happens if their system will not produce it. That is the same export versus live sync question that came up when product 3 was being reconsidered, and it now has buyer-side corroboration.
It is answerable and the answer is good, which makes it a gap in the page rather than a problem with the product.
